The second Meshu in this collection, and the more personal of the two. A woman in yellow and blue reclines against a deep crimson ground, barefoot, head tilted upward — contemplative or mid-movement, the posture suspended between rest and rhythm.

Acquired through the same African Library Project auction as the charcoal figure downstairs. The kneeling posture echoes a piece chosen the same day at the University of the Witwatersrand (Johannesburg) by a South African mentee — a work depicting a traditional Sotho dance — making this painting a quiet bridge between two friendships and two continents.

Meshu Mokitimi (b. 1926) worked across seven decades from his studio in Maseru, documenting the culture, traditions, and people of Lesotho. His work has been collected by Bill Clinton, and in 2006 King Letsie III appointed him Commander of the Most Loyal Order of Ramats’eatsana.

Acquired at auction benefiting The African Library Project — a nonprofit that has established over 4,000 libraries and placed more than one million books across sub-Saharan Africa. Meshu’s biography, A Life Lived in Love, was presented to King Letsie III at a celebration in his honor in 2016.
